response.outputText: {"title":"Lockout and Tagout in Multi-Worker Situations","question":"When several workers are isolating the same piece of equipment, what is the correct lockout and tagout procedure to ensure the equipment cannot be re-energised until every worker has finished?","answers":[{"text":"Each worker applies their own personal padlock to a multi-lock hasp, and only the worker who applied a lock may remove it.","correct":true,"feedback":"This matches the evidence: when several workers are involved, each applies their own lock to a multi-lock hasp so the equipment stays isolated until all locks are removed, and only the worker who applied a lock may remove it."},{"text":"One supervisor applies a single lock on behalf of the whole team to simplify the process.","correct":false,"feedback":"The evidence states each worker applies their own lock to a multi-lock hasp, not a single lock applied by one person for the group."},{"text":"Each worker attaches a tag without a lock, since tags alone are sufficient to warn others away from the equipment.","correct":false,"feedback":"A tag without a lock is only a warning, not a control, and must never be used alone when a lock can be fitted."},{"text":"Any worker on the team may remove another worker's lock once their own task is finished.","correct":false,"feedback":"Only the worker who applied a particular lock may remove it, regardless of whether other workers have completed their tasks."}],"evidenceIds":["ev-s15","ev-s20","ev-s21","ev-s22","ev-s24","ev-s25"]}
